app.title: PULL FOR PAIN
app.tagline: One lever. No typing. No checkbox grids.
app.deploy: static index.html at repo root, branch auto-deploys to <branch>-intake-oop.fly.dev
app.disclaimer: Fiction. LLM-generated parody patient. Not medical advice.
app.constraint: The patient cannot type and will not read a list. Every question is one reel, one lever, one answer at a time.
app.why_a_reel_beats_a_checkbox: A 15-box grid is skimmed in two seconds and answered wrong. A reel shows one option, alone, in 48px type, and will not advance until it gets an answer.

reel_modes.spin_to_pick: Reel spins through every option, lands on one. That is the answer.
reel_modes.spin_scale: Reel is 0-10. Lands on a number.

one_question_one_pull: Every question takes exactly one pull and gives exactly one answer. Seven pulls, whole intake. Nothing to grind through.

questions.care_team_note: On paper he wrote one word: 'pain'. The reel gets a sentence out of him because a sentence is the only thing on offer.
He has said 6-9 on every visit for 18 months. The number stopped carrying information a year ago. Kept because the form wants it.

questions.prompt: Besides the diabetes — what else are you being treated for?

reel.label: Something for my mood or nerves
reel.plain_language: he would never call this 'depression / anxiety'
reel.flag: He is prescribed sertraline. He did not tick this box on paper — it is printed one row below the box he did tick.

questions.care_team_note: The paper form offered 15 boxes, got 1 tick, and 2 were true. One pull, one answer — and the option is worded the way he'd say it, not the way the form prints it. 'Depression / anxiety' is a phrase he skims past. 'Something for my mood or nerves' is a phrase he answers.

questions.prompt: Any medicine that's ever made you feel bad?

flag_if_mismatch.message: Wrote 'none'. Chart has CODEINE — NAUSEA in red at the top. The word 'allergy' didn't land; 'made you feel bad' does.

questions.care_team_note: He doesn't think nausea counts as an allergy. Most people don't. Asking in plain words recovers it.

questions.prompt: Of the pills you were given — which one have you stopped, or skip?
questions.paper_answer: metformin, the nerve pill, meloxicam, tylenol

reel.label: The mood one
reel.plain_language: small white pill — he stopped it months ago
reel.flag: STOPPED. Nobody at the clinic knows. Not on his paper list — he listed four, the chart has five, this is the missing one.

reel.label: The nerve one
reel.plain_language: three a day, makes him foggy
reel.flag: Skips it on days he has things to do. Reads as non-response to treatment.

reel.label: The muscle one at night
reel.flag: Finished it in 2025. Still listed Active on the med list.

questions.care_team_note: The highest-value pull here. Asking 'which are you taking' gets a list that matches the chart. Asking which one he STOPPED gets the sertraline — the one answer nobody at the clinic has. The reel names pills the way he does, because he keeps them all in one bottle and can't tell them apart.

reel.label: Badly. For a long time now.

questions.care_team_note: He isn't sleeping and has never been asked, because the paper form has no box for it. One reel, eight seconds, and it's in the chart.

questions.prompt: Last one. What do you actually want to talk about?
questions.care_team_note: He will pick the fence. Let him. It is the only question on this form he has ever wanted to answer, and everything else comes out on the way there.

handoff.title: Three seconds before you walk in
handoff.rule: Only mismatches print. Agreement is silent.

lines.text: CODEINE allergy — he just told the machine 'nothing I know of' on paper
SERTRALINE stopped months ago. Not on his list. Still Active in your chart.
GABAPENTIN skipped on active days (foggy) — not a treatment failure, a dosing problem
Depression/anxiety never ticked on paper. Reel caught it.
Not sleeping. Never asked before today.
He wants to talk about the fence.
